title.narrative: Public Finance Management Support Programme for Ukraine (EU4PFM) Component 2 Activities Trust Fund

description.narrative:
"The EC and the WB share a common vision of building competitive and sustainable economies and in reducing poverty and social exclusion. These goals are outlined in the EU's Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) (2014-2020) - ""The EU as a global player"" and in the proposed MFF for 2021-2027 – “Neighborhood and the World”. The MFFs are designed to allow the Union to fulfil its responsibility both at global level and in its immediate neighborhoodcomma and to help safeguard global public goodscomma i.e.comma fighting poverty and promoting democracycomma peacecomma stabilitycomma and prosperity.
The MFF 2014-2020 supports the EC’s approach under the ""Agenda for Change""comma to focus EU aid in fewer sectors supportingcomma inter aliacomma good governance and creating inclusive and sustainable growth. In the context of the establishment of the Part III – EEPP programcomma it is important to take into account the new MFF which has been presented by the EC on May 2comma 2018. In factcomma the program will ideally coincide with the timeframe of the current and next proposed MFF for 2021-2027. The latter will be guided by the EU’s new consensus for developmentcomma which aims to foster sustainable development by focusing on cross-cutting elements of development policy such as gender equalitycomma youthcomma investment and tradecomma sustainable energy and climate actioncomma good governancecomma democracycomma rule of law and human rightscomma and migration and mobility.
A continued constrained growth and a tight fiscal environment in the Neighborhoodcomma Western Balkanscomma Turkeycomma and Central Asia make it important for the EC and the WB to coordinate policy advicecomma where appropriatecomma and to allocate their resources in the region in the most strategic and effective way possible. As a resultcomma the EC and the WB have begun since 2011 to interact more directly by means of a programmatic TF to support the Europe 2020 Agendacomma which has allowed the WB to engage directly with individual European countries on projects that are financed by the governments entirely or in part by EU External Action Instruments and other EU resourcescomma such as the Structural Fundscomma the Rural Development Fund or the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA).
Areas of joint cooperation and the World Bank advisory activities envisioned under the Program The EC and the WB agree that more direct interaction would be beneficial to both institutions and through them to the countries. This applies particularly to the provision of analyticalcomma advisory and knowledge servicescomma capacity and institution buildingcomma and technical assistancecomma but also to projects executed by respective governments. The EC has demonstrated its interest in specific analytical projects to be carried out by the WB which provides guidance for investments in the long-term prosperity and stability of the EU's neighborhood and support the reform process in those countries preparing for EU membership.
Areas of common interest are regularly discussed and refined on the occasion of sub-regional country day meetings between the services of the EC and WB that are held on an annual basis and reviewed by means of an annual High-Level Dialogue with DG NEAR. These meetings have focused on the Eastern Neighborhoodcomma Central Asia and Pre-Accession countriescomma and on the developmental challenges faced in the Region and which require a shared visioncomma coordinated efforts and complementarity of actions. For the current MFF 2014-2020 the instruments offered by the ECcomma and that the WB can help implement are: Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA)comma the European Neighborhood Instrument (ENI)comma the Development Cooperation Instrument (DCI)comma the Partnership Instrument (PI)comma and Macro-Financial Assistance (MFA). For the next MFF 2021-2027comma the relevant instruments will be the Neighborhoodcomma Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI - 22 billion for ECA Countries) and the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPA III – 14.5 billion).
As part of the EC - World Bank Partnership Programme Part III for Europe and Central Asia Programmatic Single-Donor Trust Fund - Livestock Sector Development Project Activitiescomma and in line with the new European Consensus on Developmentcomma the European Commission has expressed an interest in ensuring that the Bank provides support to Ukraine to better manage public resources in three specific areas of intervention including: (i) launching of a country-wide Human Resource Management Information System (HRMIS); (ii) reassessing and improving the efficiency of the Public Investment Management (PIM) system; and (iii) improving the governance of State-owned Enterprises (SOEs)."
